name: Intracranial Fast-Flow Vascular Malformation

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Intracranial Fast-Flow Vascular Malformation Diagnostic Criteria

criteria.description: Radiological evidence of fast-flow vascular malformation on MRI or angiography
Presence of neurological symptoms attributable to vascular malformation such as seizures or focal deficits
Exclusion of other vascular malformations such as cavernous malformations or venous angiomas
Histopathological confirmation if biopsy or surgery performed

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Radiological confirmation plus at least one major clinical symptom and exclusion of other vascular lesions
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis primarily relies on imaging and clinical correlation; biopsy is rarely performed.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Focal neurological deficits related to lesion location
searchTerms: weakness or numbness matching lesion site

pathognomonic.notes: May present as sudden severe headache or neurological deterioration

common.symptomName: Chronic headache localized to lesion site
Pulsatile tinnitus when lesion is near auditory structures

searchTerms: loss of part of the vision field
blind spots or missing areas in vision
cranial nerve palsies causing facial or eye problems

rare.symptomName: Hydrocephalus due to venous outflow obstruction
searchTerms: brain fluid buildup from vein blockage

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large shunts
searchTerms: heart failure from large blood shunts
heart overload due to abnormal vessels

imaging: MRI with flow-sensitive sequences showing nidus and early venous drainage
Digital subtraction angiography demonstrating arteriovenous shunting
CT scan showing hemorrhage or calcifications
other: Histopathology showing abnormal direct arteriovenous connections without intervening capillary bed

distinguishingFeatures: Low-flow vascular lesion without early venous drainage
Absence of arterial feeders on angiography
Typically presents with seizures but less often with hemorrhage
Location in dura mater rather than brain parenchyma
Often presents with pulsatile tinnitus and headache
Angiography shows fistulous connection between dural arteries and venous sinuses

redFlags: Sudden onset severe headache with neurological deterioration
New onset focal seizures in young adult
Signs of intracranial hemorrhage on imaging
references: Al-Shahi Salman R, et al. Intracranial arteriovenous malformations: diagnosis and management. Lancet Neurol. 2019.
Meyers PM, et al. Cerebral arteriovenous malformations: clinical presentation and treatment. Stroke. 2017.
